newsitem.title: INDIA: India's CARE assigns AA plus to TVS-Suzuki.
newsitem.headline: India's CARE assigns AA plus to TVS-Suzuki.

text.p: Indian credit rating firm the Credit Analysis & Research Ltd. has assigned a 'CARE AA+' Double A plus rating to the proposed one-billion-rupee Non-Convertible Debenture (NCD) issue of TVS-Suzuki Ltd.
This rating indicates that the instrument has been judged to be of high quality by all standards, and has also been classified as high investment grade, the agency said.

They are rated lower than CARE AAA securities because of somewhat lower margins of protection. Changes in assumptions may have a greater impact or the long-term risks may be somewhat larger. Overall, there is only marginal difference between the two ratings.

TSL belongs to the reputed TVS group of companies and was promoted in 1982, by Sundaram-Clayton Ltd. in collaboration with Suzuki Motor Corporation of Japan for the manufacture of motorcycles. Its product, Ind-Suzuki AX 100, was the first of the new breed o motorcycles introduced in the country.
In 1987, TSL acquired the assets of the moped division of Sundaram-Clayton Ltd, for a consideration of 310 million rupees and commenced manufacture of mopeds, CARE said.
TSL suffered losses till 1991 due to the strengthening of the yen and lack of product differentiation, which were partly offset, in later years, by the profits of the moped division.

In 1992, TSL introduced the "TVS Astra" (variomatic type), upgraded its motorcycles and introduced two new models - 'Samurai' and 'Shogun'. These vehicles were well received and the company started making profits. In November 1993, TSL, entered the scooter market with the 'TVS Scooty'.

TSL's plant is located near Hosur, Tamil Nadu with a manufacturing capacity of about 510,000 vehicles, including mopeds, motorcycles and scooters, CARE added. TSL has a market share of about 40 percent in the moped segment and about 15 percent in the motorcycle segment, but is yet to make a mark in the scooter segment.
It is the market leader in the moped segment and has a a very strong brand equity in the southern market, CARE said.
The performance of TSL over the last three years has been very good, with its turnover growing at a CARG of 52 percent, much higher than the growth rates achieved by the industry.

For FY '96, TSL earned a PAT of 352 million rupees on a turnover of 7,398 million rupees. The company's overall gearing was low at 0.41 as on March 31, 1996 and interest coverage high at 12.66 for the year ended March 31, 1996. Overall gearing would increase to about 1.67 after the proposed NCD issue.

CARE said TSL expects a significant part of its growth in future to come from the scooter segment. While TSL's "Scooty" has been well received, the company presently has no presence in the higher power, mass scooter market.

TSL now plans to manufacture scooters for the mass market, at a project cost of 16,000 million rupees, to be partly funded by the NCD issue of 1,000 million rupees, CARE said. The plant will be located near Mysore and is expected to commence production by the July 1998. Success in this segment will depend heavily on the market acceptance of the product.
CARE said the two-wheeler industry has grown at a CARG of more than 22 percent during the last three years. This high growth rates, however, may not be sustainable in the future.
